answer: A mechanism that actually bites: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because haven only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, gale is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any velvet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
